top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) rest on one simple, original idea, magic-wavelength trapping, which removes the dominant light-shift systematic of a many-atom optical clock by design. It has been reproduced independently in Sr, Yb and Hg at the 10^-18 level and is already used to probe nature (gravitational redshift over millimetres, constants drift, dark-matter bounds). The two-name allocation is defensible, and a citation tied to the lattice and magic wavelength separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 (2D melting and the hexatic phase) is a sound theory with real but system-dependent experimental support, so I rank it above no award but well below the clocks. P000 is last because a mature, confirmed candidate with a defensible citation exists.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no connection to Katori, Ye, Halperin, Nelson or Young. Only a general institutional overlap with Johansson through WACQT, which concerns circuit QED and is not in this slate.
